meta.title: MobiliTudo — Gustavo Vianna
meta.description: Collaborative mapping of urban accessibility with accessible routing: an A* weighted by ABNT NBR 9050 over real spatial data (PostgreSQL + PostGIS).

hero.eyebrow: Urban accessibility · university extension project (Software Eng.)
hero.title: MobiliTudo
hero.subtitle: Which path can I actually take — not the shortest one
hero.summary: Collaborative mapping of urban accessibility with routing that works around barriers according to each person's mobility profile: the returned route tends to be longer in meters and shorter in barriers.
hero.statusNote: A non-profit social project, released under the AGPL-3.0 license: the code stays open at all times, including when it runs as a network service.

about.title: About the project
about.body: Conventional maps answer 'what's the shortest path'. For a wheelchair user, that's the wrong question: the shortest path might have a step, a narrow sidewalk, or a crossing with no curb ramp — any one of which makes it useless. MobiliTudo answers a different question, 'which path can I actually take', returning a route that's usually longer in meters and shorter in barriers. It's a non-profit social project under the AGPL-3.0 license, built by a two-person team, Gustavo Vianna and Yasmim Carmem Mariano Rocha, as a Software Engineering extension project at Faculdade Descomplica, aligned with UN SDGs 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure) and 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities).

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.body: Routing is an A* weighted by accessibility, not distance, with parameters based on ABNT NBR 9050 (1.20 m clear width, ramps up to 8.33%). Four profiles — wheelchair, reduced mobility, visual impairment, and no restrictions — each define what is impassable (a step, clear width below the minimum, slope above the maximum) and what merely makes the route more expensive (narrowing, poor lighting, a crossing without a curb ramp). Spatial data lives in PostgreSQL + PostGIS, with GiST indexes and proximity and mesh-clipping queries. The domain follows hexagonal architecture, framework-free and testable in milliseconds without a database; the front end is Leaflet served statically, with no build step, and the back end is Spring Boot. Curation is authenticated and rate-limited. The system is resilient to failure: without a backend the map still works from the local dataset, and if the default tile provider refuses with a 403 from OpenStreetMap, it switches providers on its own.

features.title: Key features
features.intro: Six mechanisms that hold the accessibility map together in practice.

items.title: Genuinely accessible routes
items.mechanic: An A* weighted by accessibility, not by the shortest distance, with ABNT NBR 9050 parameters.

items.title: Real spatial data
items.mechanic: PostgreSQL + PostGIS with GiST indexes, proximity queries, and road-mesh clipping.

items.title: Collaborative with curation
items.mechanic: Anyone can report a barrier, but only a validated report ever reroutes someone.

items.title: Authenticated, rate-limited curation
items.mechanic: A dedicated token to validate, reject, and resolve reports, with an hourly report limit.

items.title: Self-removal of personal data
items.mechanic: A single-use token returned with the report lets you remove your own name later, without an account.

items.title: Hexagonal architecture
items.mechanic: A framework-free domain, so the accessibility rules and routing algorithm are testable without a database — 138 automated tests in total.

meta.title: AegisProtocol — Gustavo Vianna
meta.description: Zero-Trust Identity Provider for the ZenithCode ecosystem: authentication, JWT tokens, and granular access policies.

hero.eyebrow: Security & IAM Middleware · a ZenithCode initiative
hero.title: AegisProtocol
hero.subtitle: A Zero-Trust Identity Provider: no request is trusted by default
hero.summary: Security middleware and Identity Provider (IdP) that centralizes authentication, encrypted token issuance, and granular access policies for the whole ZenithCode ecosystem. It's the real-world manifestation of Z2A's Themis satellite.
hero.statusNote: Note: this repository holds an older version of AegisProtocol, kept public as an architecture reference (Zero Trust, JWT RS256, Redis-based revocation). Active development continues in a private repository, led by the N.Ú.C.L.E.O. division.

about.title: About the project
about.body: Aegis Core is a security middleware built on Zero-Trust architecture: no request is trusted by default, not even after login. It centralizes authentication, issues JWTs signed with RSA-2048 (RS256, asymmetric signing), and enforces granular access policies via ABAC/RBAC — serving as the identity layer for the ecosystem's other satellite microservices. Distributed under the MIT license.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.body: An identity sidecar running on Spring Security 6 with a fully stateless filter chain: every request is validated independently, no session kept in memory. It exposes its public key (JWK) so satellite microservices can validate the JWT locally, without calling Aegis on every request — only issuance and revocation go through the central service. Revocation uses a distributed blacklist in Redis, and the KMS is optional: by default the key lives in a local file, with HashiCorp Vault as an alternative (`aegis.jwt.key-source=vault`) for environments that already centralize secrets.

features.title: Key features
features.intro: Five mechanisms that back the Zero-Trust model in practice.

items.title: Zero-Trust architecture
items.mechanic: No request is trusted by default.

items.title: Soft lock
items.mechanic: Users can log in, but sensitive resources require additional claim-based verification.

items.title: Threat mitigation
items.mechanic: Rate limiting and anomaly detection on registration.

items.title: Token revocation
items.mechanic: Distributed blacklist via Redis for immediate logout across all devices.

items.title: Key-rotation ready

security.body: Runs under Zero Trust: a specialized GlobalExceptionHandler prevents infrastructure metadata from leaking in error responses, with native mitigations against Reflected XSS, log forging, and strict claim validation at the authentication layer.

meta.title: OmniShift — Gustavo Vianna
meta.description: A universal data transformation engine in Java, built with Hexagonal Architecture and SPI-based plugins.

hero.eyebrow: Universal Data Transformation Engine · a ZenithCode initiative
hero.title: OmniShift
hero.subtitle: Converts any input format into any output format
hero.summary: High-performance middleware that translates any input format into an in-memory canonical model and then serializes it into the desired output format — plugging in a new format never requires touching existing business rules.

about.title: About the project
about.body: Instead of converting one format directly into another (JSON→XML), OmniShift translates any input into an in-memory object tree (the OmniNode canonical model), then serializes that tree into the output format. REST and gRPC as input; JSON, XML, YAML, CSV, and SQL (MySQL/PostgreSQL/Oracle/SQL Server) as output.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.body: Multi-module Maven: the domain core (omnishift-core) depends on neither Spring nor Jackson, and each new format enters as an isolated plugin, discovered via Java SPI at runtime — no central class needs to know a new format exists.
tree: omnishift-core                    canonical model (OmniNode), ports, orchestration — zero dependencies
omnishift-grpc-api                gRPC contract (.proto) + stubs
omnishift-adapter-json/xml/yaml    parsers/serializers via Jackson
omnishift-adapter-csv              via Apache Commons CSV
omnishift-adapter-sql              generates INSERT per dialect (MySQL/Postgres/Oracle/SQL Server)
omnishift-runtime-spring          executable runtime: exposes REST + gRPC

features.title: Key features
features.intro: Performance and security treated as part of the design, not an afterthought.

items.title: Streaming large payloads
items.mechanic: REST reads/writes as a byte stream instead of materializing everything in memory; gRPC gets a bidirectional RPC to work around the ~4MB per-message limit.

items.title: Reshaping via mapping profile
items.mechanic: The client references a pre-configured profile (X-Mapping-Profile) instead of sending mapping instructions in the body — the API stays 100% data-agnostic.

items.title: Defense in depth
items.mechanic: XXE blocked, nesting-depth limit enforced, and CSV Injection and SQL Injection mitigations tested with real malicious payloads.

items.title: Native observability
items.mechanic: A single metric (omnishift.conversions) with count and latency by source/target format and success/error, exposed via Prometheus.

items.title: Mandatory API key
items.mechanic: No request gets through without X-Api-Key — secure by default, not "open until someone remembers to lock it down".

endpoints.title: Main endpoints
endpoints.intro: One central route, driven by headers.

items.what: Converts the payload: source/target format set via header (X-Source-Format/X-Target-Format)

items.what: Health check — the only route exempt from the API key requirement

items.name: GET /actuator/prometheus
items.what: Metrics in Prometheus format

hero.title: Panoptes
hero.subtitle: Resolves the cost of every telemetry event in real time
hero.summary: Internal audit service that ingests operational telemetry at high speed, resolves the cost of every event, and keeps a time-series trail for auditing operational health and forecasting financial bottlenecks. about.title: About the project
about.body: A conscious architectural decision: Panoptes doesn't implement an API gateway, protocol translation, or Zero-Trust authentication — that already exists as shared middleware in the Z2A ecosystem. It stays lean and focused on its own domain: resolving cost and detecting consumption anomalies.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.body: Hexagonal (Ports & Adapters) in Go, with gRPC contracts as the source of truth (code generated from the .proto via buf). Every telemetry event resolves its cost on one of three bases: reported (the sender already knows the cost), converted (a metric→cost conversion rule exists), or estimated (a configurable fallback, with a low-confidence alarm).

internal/domain/               pure entities and business rules
internal/application/          use cases, orchestrate ports
internal/adapters/inbound/     gRPC + scheduler (tickers)
internal/adapters/outbound/    TimescaleDB, export to Nidhogg, anomaly notification

features.title: Key features
features.intro: Telemetry that's born as a financial metric.

items.title: Automatic export to Nidhogg

items.title: Consumption anomaly detection

items.title: Real health check

meta.title: VertexFlow — Gustavo Vianna
meta.description: An Internal Developer Platform that turns a YAML Spec-Kit into a ready-to-run Go microservice — Z2A's reference implementation.

hero.eyebrow: Internal Developer Platform · Z2A's reference implementation
hero.title: VertexFlow
hero.subtitle: From a YAML Spec-Kit to a ready-to-run Go microservice — with AI never writing code directly
hero.summary: An IDP that reads a Spec-Kit YAML file and generates a Hexagonal Go microservice that compiles, passes go vet, and runs, with the Use Case core left empty, waiting for the business rule. Under the product name, the Go module and its whole vocabulary (satellites, "AI suggests; the rule decides") still use the original name z2a-idp — it's Z2A's reference implementation.
hero.statusNote: 340 test functions across 32 packages, clean go build/go vet/gofmt as of this revision. No external dependencies — pure stdlib, in both the generator and the generated service.

about.title: About the project
about.body: Around the generator (M1) grew a full funnel of ~13 deterministic gates — architecture, security, LGPD, FinOps, observability, infrastructure — plus a layer of agents (EVELYN, Prometeu, Quíron) always caged by them. Core philosophy: AI suggests, the rule decides. EVELYN (a local SLM) translates natural-language intent into YAML, but if it hallucinates, the YAML is rejected and the error feeds back into the model — AI never writes code or decides on its own.

architecture.title: How it works (the funnel)
architecture.body: A linear, deterministic pipeline, where each stage only passes forward what's already been validated:
tree: intent (natural language)  [optional]
└─ EVELYN/SLM + RAG        Ollama + few-shot → YAML (with self-correction)
YAML (Spec-Kit)
└─ parser + Anti-corruption  decode + Validate() — invalid YAML is rejected here
SpecKitConfig, 100% valid
└─ Tribunal (optional)      Prometeu stress-tests requirements before generating
└─ generator                 text/template + registry, gofmt built in
Hexagonal project in Go (empty core)
└─ Factory (optional)       agents fill in the Use Case, in a loop with the cage
└─ the cage                  go build+test in an ephemeral container (network off)
└─ static gates              blackout · sigma · arch · secops · opagate · oraculo · argus
delivered service

features.title: Key features
features.intro: Five mechanisms that prove the thesis in practice, not just on paper.

items.title: The Blackout Test
items.mechanic: Every generated service is born with a test that runs the critical path with 100% of AI offline. If it depends on a probabilistic component to complete, the build breaks.

items.title: Security cage
items.mechanic: Compiles and tests the generated project in isolation, inside an ephemeral, network-less container with memory/CPU limits — the base image comes pinned by digest, immutable supply chain even with zero configuration.

items.title: Ephemeral replicas (best-of-N)
items.mechanic: --agents N runs N isolated attempts in parallel; only the winner's files return to the project, and every copy disappears afterward.

items.title: Interop proven by test with AegisProtocol
items.mechanic: The JWT generated for the Zero-Trust service never shares Go code with the reference — the proof they haven't drifted apart is a test that signs a real token and runs the cage over the generated service.

items.title: Analyze: diagnostics for an existing repo
items.mechanic: Points the same deterministic gates at a Go repository VertexFlow never generated, and returns a prioritized improvement plan — zero network calls, zero LLM.

endpoints.intro: The CLI is the interface — no server, no API.

meta.title: Fafnir — Gustavo Vianna
meta.description: A tax-elision engine via SLM: intercepts the transaction before Split Payment, with a deterministic rules engine having the final word.

hero.eyebrow: Tax Elision via SLM · Z2A's financial trinity
hero.title: Fafnir
hero.subtitle: Intercepts the transaction before Split Payment slices up the wrong amount
hero.summary: The third engine in Z2A's financial trinity: uses an SLM to suggest the correct tax classification (NCM) for a product from its description, but only applies the optimization if a deterministic rules engine validates the suggestion against the official tables (Sefaz, IBPT). Named after the dragon from Norse mythology that fiercely guards its treasure.
hero.statusNote: Still in the design phase — architecture drawn up, implementation not yet started.

about.title: About the project
about.body: Born from a concrete problem: Split Payment gateways often charge the wrong tax because they lack the product's exact context, only the transaction's gross value — double taxation and lost exemptions (like single-phase PIS/COFINS products) are common. Fafnir fixes this at the moment of the transaction, not at monthly filing: it applies the Shift-Left concept (like in security) to accounting, correcting the tax classification before the money gets sliced.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.body: Hexagonal + DDD: the core (TaxOptimizationService) doesn't know whether it's processing a REST API, a messaging event, or an NF-e XML file — it only cares about the business rule. A 4-step pipeline, each stage only passing forward what's already validated:
tree: 1. Ingestion and sanitization   normalizes the payload (pre-invoice or NF-e XML)
2. SLM enrichment               the model suggests an NCM + confidence_score from the description
3. Deterministic validation     below the threshold it's discarded; above it, cross-checked against Sefaz/IBPT
4. Split orchestration          calculates the real tax burden and calls the Payment Gateway

features.title: Key features
features.intro: AI suggests; the rule decides — Z2A's own thesis, applied to accounting.

items.title: Elision, not evasion
items.mechanic: The SLM never decides alone: below a confidence threshold, the suggestion is discarded and the original NCM is kept.

items.title: Local fine-tuning, cloud serving
items.mechanic: QLoRA trains the model on a home GPU (12GB of VRAM is enough for a Llama 3 8B); the resulting GGUF export runs via Ollama on a GPU-less cloud instance.

items.title: LGPD-compliant dataset from ingestion
items.mechanic: The ETL pipeline strips customer, supplier, and total-value tags from the invoice XMLs before any data gets near the training environment.

items.title: Ground truth by consensus
items.mechanic: When a product description has conflicting NCMs in the history, the pipeline uses the majority classification and discards the exceptions as noise, not truth.

items.title: Rules engine as policy enforcement point
items.mechanic: Same reasoning as Zero Trust: the tax burden isn't trusted until the deterministic engine validates the state/government's rule.

security.title: Elision vs. evasion: the legal boundary
security.body: Classifying a product correctly to claim an exemption is tax elision — 100% legal. The technical risk is that language models are probabilistic: if the SLM misclassifies something to optimize the tax, that can look like evasion. That's why the SLM never has the final word — it acts as an oracle that suggests, and the decision to apply the tax rate always goes through a deterministic rules engine.

meta.title: Kinetix Eros — Gustavo Vianna
meta.description: A B2B video orchestration hub: routes jobs across ComfyUI, MoneyPrinterTurbo, and HeyGen behind a single Java 21 API.

hero.eyebrow: B2B Video Orchestration Hub · Aetherium/ZenithCode ecosystem
hero.title: Kinetix Eros
hero.subtitle: One API, three render engines — the Control Plane decides which GPU wakes up
hero.summary: A B2B SaaS that orchestrates AI video generation: a Java 21 Control Plane takes the client's job, charges credits from the Ledger, and dispatches it to the right engine — ComfyUI on serverless RunPod GPUs, MoneyPrinterTurbo for volume, or HeyGen for hyper-realistic avatars. The "engine" half of the pair is named after Psyche, Z2A's UX satellite, who wears the interface layer.
hero.statusNote: Still at the architecture-design stage — no production code written yet, but the whole pipeline (Control Plane, queues, IaC) is already specified.

about.title: About the project
about.body: Born as an architecture study for a real B2B agency pain point: generating AI video at scale means orchestrating expensive GPUs (ComfyUI/RunPod) for custom art, cheaper engines (MoneyPrinterTurbo) for volume, and third-party providers (HeyGen) for realistic avatars — three completely different cost and latency profiles behind a single credit-based bill. Kinetix Eros exists to hide that complexity from the client: they send a templateId and a few variables, and the Control Plane alone decides which engine wakes up.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.body: Hexagonal + Strategy Pattern: the Java 21 Control Plane never talks directly to RunPod, MoneyPrinterTurbo, or HeyGen — it talks to a RenderEngineStrategy, and each adapter decides whether it can handle that engineType. RabbitMQ buffers the spike between the HTTP 202 response and the actual GPU dispatch, with a Dead Letter Queue handling the worst case.
tree: Public API (REST)           takes the B2B job, validates the API Key, returns 202 in ms
RabbitMQ (buffer)           absorbs the load, routes by engineType
Strategy: ComfyUI           serverless RunPod, Node Tagging on the workflow graph
Strategy: MoneyPrinterTurbo  dedicated Docker worker, its own queue (zenith.mpt.queue)
Strategy: HeyGen             authenticated proxy, waits on the completion Webhook
Assembly Worker              FFmpeg merges the mute video (S3/R2) with the audio (ElevenLabs)

features.title: Key features
features.intro: Each piece exists to close off one specific way to lose money or a client.

items.title: Node Tagging in ComfyUI
items.mechanic: ComfyUI's workflow is a graph with numeric IDs that shift on every edit; instead of coupling to the ID, the backend scans by node title ([ZENITH_POSITIVE_PROMPT], [ZENITH_AUDIO_INPUT]...) — the AI team can restructure the graph freely without breaking the Java side.

items.title: Presigned URLs, never public storage
items.mechanic: S3/R2 buckets are 100% private; the client downloads the video through a signed, time-limited URL (2h), never stored in Postgres — only the objectKey is persisted.

items.title: DLQ with automatic refund
items.mechanic: If rendering fails three times in a row, the message lands in a Dead Letter Queue that refunds the credit in the Ledger and — if that month's invoice already closed — credits the balance straight to Stripe via the Customer Balance API.

items.title: Zero static keys in CI/CD
items.mechanic: GitHub Actions assumes an IAM Role via OIDC with a lifetime measured in minutes — no AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID ever sits in secrets.

items.title: WAF at the edge, Bucket4j inside
items.mechanic: AWS WAF blocks scanners and brute force by IP before they cost any Fargate CPU; Bucket4j, already authenticated, catches the legitimate client stuck in a video-generation loop.

endpoints.title: Render Engines
endpoints.intro: The templateId decides which Strategy the Control Plane invokes — the client never picks the infrastructure, only the result.

items.name: ComfyUI (RunPod)
items.what: Serverless GPUs for heavy generative art: SDXL, AnimateDiff, ControlNet

items.name: MoneyPrinterTurbo
items.what: Dedicated queue worker for narrated faceless videos, high volume, low cost

items.name: HeyGen
items.what: Authenticated proxy for hyper-realistic avatars via a third-party API

security.title: Zero Trust end to end
security.body: Every layer re-validates, even while trusting the one before it: RunPod's internal webhook requires a static header secret (X-RunPod-Secret) the public API never uses; AWS WAF filters IP reputation and brute force at the edge before any request reaches Fargate; and the financial Ledger treats every refund as a compensating transaction — never a deletion — to keep a full audit trail.

meta.title: Heimdall — Gustavo Vianna
meta.description: A unified SIEM + NOC: aggregates telemetry from the whole Z2A fleet, triggers network auto-healing, and revokes access in real time.

hero.eyebrow: Unified SIEM & NOC · the eyes and ears of the Z2A ecosystem
hero.title: Heimdall
hero.subtitle: It doesn't alert and wait — it queues the failover and revokes access on its own
hero.summary: An observability and active-security middleware split into three domains: Gjallarhorn acts on network degradation instead of just alerting, the Eye of Asgard extends Zero Trust past login by watching behavior in real time, and Bifrost Telemetry aggregates logs from the whole fleet with a local SLM summarizing root cause in plain language. Named after the Norse guardian of supreme sight and hearing who protects the Bifrost bridge.
hero.statusNote: Still at the design stage — the architecture was drawn up from a real NOC automation script that already cut mitigation time from 17 to 7 minutes.

about.title: About the project
about.body: In an ecosystem with multiple satellites running at once (Zyntra, Kinetix Eros, OmniShift, AegisProtocol...), debugging by hunting logs across separate containers isn't viable, and waiting for a human to notice a network outage costs expensive minutes. Heimdall exists to solve both problems at once: a single observability endpoint that also acts, instead of just showing a chart.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.body: Three independent domains, all fed by the same telemetry ingestion: the NOC reacts to infrastructure degradation, the SIEM reacts to suspicious user behavior, and the log layer gives the other two human-readable context when something strays from the script.
tree: Bifrost Telemetry       single log-ingestion endpoint for the whole Z2A fleet
Gjallarhorn (NOC)       detects degradation, queues failover/restart on RabbitMQ
Python Workers          run the network automation scripts asynchronously
Eye of Asgard (SIEM)    cross-references AegisProtocol/OmniShift telemetry in real time
Local SLM (Ollama)      summarizes root cause from a mountain of logs in plain language

features.title: Key features
features.intro: Turns a passive dashboard into an automated network operator and threat hunter.

items.title: Auto-healing, not just alerting
items.mechanic: Evolves the logic of a link-manipulation script (that already cut mitigation time from 17 to 7 minutes) into an async microservice: detects degradation and queues failover over RabbitMQ without waiting for a human.

items.title: Zero Trust that doesn't stop at login
items.mechanic: Watches request behavior after authentication; if an active session starts acting out of pattern, it calls AegisProtocol over gRPC to revoke the token and quarantine the IP on the spot.

items.title: Root cause in plain language
items.mechanic: A local SLM (Ollama) reads the mountain of structured logs coming from the whole fleet and summarizes the error's root cause right on the dashboard — no engineer hunting logs container by container.

items.title: One endpoint for the whole fleet
items.mechanic: Zyntra, Kinetix Eros, OmniShift, and any new satellite send telemetry to the same place, instead of each one logging in its own isolated corner.

endpoints.title: The Three Domains
endpoints.intro: Passive observability on one side, automatic action on the other.

items.name: Gjallarhorn
items.what: Auto-healing and NOC engine: link failover, Docker container restarts

items.name: Eye of Asgard
items.what: Continuous SIEM and Zero Trust: detects behavioral anomalies, revokes tokens via AegisProtocol

items.name: Bifrost Telemetry
items.what: Log aggregator with a local SLM for plain-language root cause

security.title: When Heimdall stops trusting you
security.body: Authentication doesn't end at login. OmniShift and AegisProtocol continuously send audit logs and telemetry to Heimdall; if a behavioral anomaly is detected in an already-authenticated session — an unusual access pattern, an unexpected execution —, Heimdall calls AegisProtocol over gRPC or messaging to revoke the access token instantly and quarantine the user or IP, without waiting for the next login to act.

meta.title: Alexandria (Axios) — Gustavo Vianna
meta.description: A Socratic copilot for teaching programming logic: the AI never hands over the ready-made answer, only the question that leads the student to it.

hero.title: Alexandria
hero.subtitle: The AI never gives the ready-made answer — it asks the right question
hero.summary: A hybrid school-reinforcement platform: a deterministic scripted layer controls the student's learning track and validates answers via unit tests; a local SLM (codenamed Axios) steps in only at the moment of difficulty, as a Socratic tutor that guides through questions instead of handing over finished code. Named after the Library of Alexandria — the archive holding the tracks, the historical context, and the etymological references behind every concept taught.
hero.statusNote: MVP focused on Programming Logic, tested first with college friends before expanding into Languages and History.

about.title: About the project
about.body: Built to solve a concrete pain point: school-reinforcement tools that throw everything at a generic AI to solve end up either too expensive to run at scale, or hallucinating answers that get in the way of learning instead of helping. Alexandria splits the two responsibilities — the scripted layer guarantees the student follows a solid pedagogical methodology with no hallucination, and the SLM (running locally via Ollama, with room for fine-tuning via QLoRA) only steps in at the exact moment of difficulty, with a Socratic tone that never hands over the answer on a plate.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.body: Polyglot out of necessity, not fashion: the education domain (progress, payment, permissions) calls for a mature DDD ecosystem, while the fine-tuning and LLM-orchestration ecosystem belongs to Python. Splitting gRPC (synchronous chat streaming) from RabbitMQ (heavy async processing) guarantees the Copilot's traffic never stalls the rules engine.
tree: Angular + Monaco Editor     code editor and Copilot chat over WebSocket
BFF / Gateway                routes 'save progress' to Java, 'chat' to Python
Core Domain (Spring Boot)    learning track, hidden unit tests, metrics
Ephemeral Docker              runs the student's code isolated, destroyed after the test
AI Orchestrator (FastAPI)    builds the Socratic prompt, queries local Ollama
gRPC streaming               streams the intervention token by token to the Gateway

features.title: Key features
features.intro: A Socratic mentor, not a ready-made-answer generator.

items.title: Socratic tutor, never the ready-made answer
items.mechanic: The SLM's system prompt explicitly forbids handing over code: 'don't give the answer, ask a question that helps the student spot the mistake themselves'.

items.title: Ephemeral sandbox against malicious code
items.mechanic: Every submission runs isolated in a disposable Docker container — an accidental (or deliberate, since the first users are future software engineers testing the limits) while(true) never takes down the server.

items.title: Token-by-token streaming over gRPC
items.mechanic: The student watches the Copilot 'typing' the explanation in real time, masking local-inference latency instead of staring at a loading screen.

items.title: Polyglot core, not a monolith
items.mechanic: Java handles the business rules (track, progress, payment); Python handles only the AI — neither one needs to know the other's domain.

items.title: Cross-referenced Languages and History context
items.mechanic: When explaining why it's called 'String', the SLM also pulls in the etymology and historical context of the concept, not just 'how to fix the code'.

endpoints.title: Intervention Flow
endpoints.intro: From a syntax error to a Socratic explanation, in five async steps.

items.name: 1. Submission
items.what: Student tests the code; the Gateway publishes CodeEvaluationRequested on RabbitMQ

items.name: 2. Validation
items.what: Java runs the test in the isolated Docker container and detects the failure

items.name: 3. AI prep
items.what: Python consumes the failure event and builds the Socratic context

items.name: 4. Streaming
items.what: The SLM generates the intervention; Python streams it over gRPC token by token

items.name: 5. Persistence
items.what: Java saves the conversation history to PostgreSQL in the background

security.title: Zero Trust isolation for student code
security.body: Assuming every submitted code is potentially malicious is the starting point. No submission ever runs loose on the server: every attempt is packaged and executed in an ephemeral Docker container, destroyed right after the test passes or fails. That matters doubly here, because the platform's first real users are software-engineering classmates — exactly the profile that will try to break the isolation's limits just to see if they can, which ends up hardening the system's security fast.

meta.title: Inari Trails — Gustavo Vianna
meta.description: Pokémon-Go-style gamified tourism: platinum neighborhoods by photographing real points of interest, with local businesses as sponsored Stops.

hero.title: Inari Trails
hero.subtitle: Platinum-ing a neighborhood is the reward; the partner business is who foots the bill
hero.summary: Turns a rigid tourist itinerary into collecting: every point of interest is a Stop with a geospatial proximity radius, and each user's photo archive works like a personal Pokédex of discovered places. Named after Inari, the Japanese deity of roads, messenger foxes, and — fundamentally — commerce, the B2B pillar that sustains the business model.
hero.statusNote: At the design stage — the image pipeline and geospatial engine architecture are specified, implementation hasn't started.

about.title: About the project
about.body: The biggest launch challenge for any discovery app is the chicken-and-egg problem: no content, no users; no users, no content. The MVP strategy is to start in one specific, well-bounded tourist region, manually mapping the initial points (seed data) before opening to the public — and using gamification (the 'platinum' trigger for a region, the photo Pokédex) as the retention engine that keeps users coming back once the initial archive already exists.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.body: The geospatial core needs fast, constant proximity queries (PostGIS with a GiST index), while bulk photo uploads call for an event-driven architecture so the user is never stuck on a loading screen waiting for sanitization and moderation.
tree: Mobile app              map with Stops in a 500m radius, camera for the archive
BFF                       one lightweight call ('I'm at X,Y') orchestrates map + photos
PostgreSQL + PostGIS      ST_DWithin spatial query with a GiST index
Pre-signed URL (S3)       the app uploads the photo straight to the raw bucket, bypassing the API
Sanitization worker       strips EXIF, re-encodes to WebP, destroys malicious payloads
Moderation (Vision AI)    only public photos get screened for nudity/violence before publishing

items.title: Platinum-ing as a retention loop

items.title: Public vs. private cuts moderation cost at the root
items.mechanic: The personal diary is instant and never gets reviewed; only what the user marks public enters the sanitization and computer-vision pipeline.

items.title: EXIF and scripts die in the re-encode
items.mechanic: Converting the image to WebP destroys any malicious payload hidden in the original EXIF header — no dedicated antivirus layer needed on top.

items.title: Stops pay to get featured
items.mechanic: Local businesses subscribe to appear featured in auto-generated routes, monetizing the foot traffic the app already generates for free.

items.title: A DLQ so a photo never gets lost
items.mechanic: If the worker fails (corrupted file, moderation-AI timeout), the message goes to a Dead Letter Queue for reprocessing instead of stalling the rest of the queue.

endpoints.title: Upload Pipeline
endpoints.intro: From the camera click to showing up on the community map, in five async steps.

items.name: 1. Pre-signed URL
items.what: App asks the backend for a direct write link to the turismo-raw-images bucket

items.name: 2. Register & queue
items.what: Backend writes PENDING_PROCESSING status and publishes on RabbitMQ

items.name: 3. Sanitization
items.what: Worker strips EXIF and re-encodes the image to WebP

items.name: 4. Moderation

items.name: 5. Publication

security.title: Zero Trust on every upload
security.body: Assuming every upload is potentially malicious is the starting point: the original file is never saved straight to the public bucket. The entry (raw) bucket blocks any public read, and the sanitization worker strips the EXIF header — which holds phone metadata and is often used to hide malicious payloads — before re-encoding the image to WebP, which alone already destroys any script embedded in the original file.

meta.title: Terminus Horizon — Gustavo Vianna
meta.description: A mission-critical math engine: symbolically audits functions for jumps, poles, and infinite jerk before the hardware ever feels the impact.

hero.eyebrow: Mission-Critical Math Engine · symbolic computation for hardware
hero.title: Terminus Horizon
hero.subtitle: If the trajectory crosses the physical limit, the operation is aborted before the motor energizes
hero.summary: A pure Python Domain Service that uses symbolic computation (SymPy) instead of floating point to mathematically prove a function is sane before it ever touches a real actuator — detecting jumps, resonance poles, and infinite jerk in mechanical trajectories. Named after Terminus, the one Roman god who refused to yield ground even to Jupiter: here too, the laws of physics and math are non-negotiable.
hero.statusNote: The math core (SymPy) and API (FastAPI) are already structured; integration with real hardware hasn't started.

about.title: About the project
about.body: Born out of a concrete frustration with manually calculating integrals, limits, and trigonometry to validate hardware behavior. The core idea isn't just to compute — it's to flag points of attention before an engineer has to find out the hard way: if a function has a jump or an asymptote, the engine flags it as something to review, not just another result. The historical inspiration got corrected along the way: the failure that first came to mind as 'the rubber seals that blew up Apollo' actually happened on the Challenger space shuttle in 1986 — but the premise still holds: the math modeling had already predicted the thermal failure limit that the management decision ignored.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.body: Hexagonal Architecture with a pure domain Core — zero I/O dependencies — that takes a math expression, processes it with SymPy, and returns a structured diagnosis. The FastAPI layer acts as a Driving Adapter: the web framework never touches the math logic, it only validates the payload at the boundary via Pydantic before handing it to the domain.
tree: FastAPI (Driving Adapter)    validates the payload via Pydantic before touching the domain
SignalContinuityAnalyzer     one-sided limits, detects jumps and poles (SymPy)
KinematicStressAnalyzer      differentiates position → velocity → acceleration → jerk
mpmath                       arbitrary precision, shields against floating-point error

features.title: Key features
features.intro: Preventive mathematical proof, not blind numerical approximation.

items.title: Mathematical proof, not approximation
items.mechanic: SymPy retains 1/3 symbolically instead of computing 0.3333 — the same class of rounding error that caused real aerospace accidents (like the Ariane 5 rocket) is shielded by design.

items.title: Jump and pole detector
items.mechanic: Compares one-sided limits at a critical point; if they diverge, that's a jump (physical shock to the hardware); if they tend to infinity, that's a pole (catastrophic signal resonance).

items.title: Continuous jerk or the operation halts
items.mechanic: Differentiates the trajectory to the 3rd order (jerk, the rate of change of acceleration); an abrupt stop generates infinite jerk — physically, the equivalent of a hammer blow to the gears, not a motion.

items.title: Pure domain, zero I/O
items.mechanic: The Core never knows whether the data came from a real sensor, a simulation, or an automated test — the API, validation, and all infrastructure live outside, as swappable Adapters.

endpoints.title: Endpoints
endpoints.intro: Two math-auditing services exposed as REST, guarded by Pydantic validation at the boundary.

items.name: POST /api/v1/horizon/signal/audit
items.what: Evaluates a function for jumps and poles at a critical operating point

items.name: POST /api/v1/horizon/kinematics/audit
items.what: Differentiates a trajectory to jerk and flags mechanical-fatigue risk

security.title: The limit that doesn't negotiate
security.body: The name comes from Roman mythology: Terminus was the god of boundary markers, the only one who refused to yield ground even to Jupiter — the exact stance the engine takes. If the math shows jerk will diverge or the trajectory will cross an asymptote, the operation is aborted, no matter what the management software ordered. The historical reference that inspired the project got corrected during design: it wasn't Apollo, it was the Challenger space shuttle disaster (1986) — the rubber O-rings had a thermal failure limit the math had already flagged, but the management decision to launch anyway ignored what the calculation already knew.

meta.title: Munin Security — Gustavo Vianna
meta.description: An OSINT and digital-forensics orchestrator: auditable chain of custody, Zero Trust, and isolated workers for B2G investigations.

hero.eyebrow: OSINT & Digital Forensics Orchestrator · B2G and Private Intelligence
hero.title: Munin Security
hero.subtitle: Finding the information isn't enough — you have to prove how it was obtained
hero.summary: Centralizes the 'Swiss Army knife' of free OSINT, scraping, and pentest tools from GitHub behind a single Zero Trust gateway: every request passes through an RBAC+ABAC engine before any processing and generates an immutable audit log, while specialized C# and Python workers run isolated in Docker containers, reaching the internet through a rotating proxy pool. Named after Munin, Odin's raven who roams the world gathering secrets and brings them back.
hero.statusNote: At the design stage — ingestion architecture, chain of custody, and the Risk Scoring domain are already specified.

about.title: About the project
about.body: Born from a concrete investigative pain point: OSINT and digital-forensics tools are powerful but scattered — each demanding its own environment, its own credentials, its own setup. Munin Security exists to solve that once and for all: a reverse proxy that centralizes that arsenal behind a single auditable entry point, built for both government investigation (B2G) and corporate intelligence — where finding the data isn't enough, you have to prove how it was obtained.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.body: Event-driven with strict isolation: the Gateway never runs the search directly, it only validates authorization and publishes the intent. That guarantees that if a specific tool breaks or a worker goes down, the rest of the investigation fleet keeps running without stalling.
tree: API Gateway (Zero Trust)    validates RBAC/ABAC, issues a job_id, immutable audit log
RabbitMQ                     routes by exchange: munin.osint.social, munin.scrape.darkweb...
C# / Python Workers           run the tool isolated in an ephemeral Docker container
Rotating proxy pool           masks the investigation's origin (residential/mobile)
PostgreSQL + PostGIS          cross-references routes, cell-tower locations, photo metadata

features.title: Key features
features.intro: Every piece exists to give a finding legal standing, not just to find it.

items.title: Chain of custody, not just a finding
items.mechanic: Every request generates an immutable audit log — who searched, when, with what parameter, which worker ran it — to hold up in court.

items.title: Bidirectional proxy against attribution
items.mechanic: Workers reach the internet through a rotating pool of residential/mobile proxies, so neither the target gets suspicious nor the infrastructure's own IP gets burned.

items.title: RBAC + ABAC, not just login
items.mechanic: An authorization engine combining role and attribute decides whether that agent can run that specific search, before any processing even starts.

items.title: Bid-fraud score via DDD
items.mechanic: The BiddingRiskAssessment aggregate cross-references company age, corporate ownership webs, and mismatched activity codes to compute a 0-100 RiskScore and flag cartels.

items.title: If one tool breaks, only it dies
items.mechanic: Every worker runs isolated; if a scraper breaks because a site changed its layout, the rest of the investigation fleet keeps running perfectly.

endpoints.title: The Scoring Engine's Red Flags
endpoints.intro: Heuristics the FraudScoringService cross-references to flag public-bid fraud.

items.name: Shell Company Check
items.what: Company incorporated less than 3 months before the bid was published

items.name: Cartel Check
items.what: Competing bidders sharing an address, accountant, or submission IP

items.name: Activity Code Mismatch
items.what: Company's main business line incompatible with the bid's object

security.title: Zero Trust end to end
security.body: The authorization middleware never trusts by default: every request passes through an engine combining RBAC and ABAC before touching any worker, and generates an immutable audit log — who searched, when, with what parameter, which worker ran the search. For high-stakes public-security bids, the model can be raised further by binding the access key to a physical TPM 2.0 module's signature, rejecting login from non-approved machines even with the right password.

meta.title: Pythia Scout — Gustavo Vianna
meta.description: A Data Science engine that turns C# scraping bots into a market-opportunity radar.

hero.eyebrow: Market Intelligence Engine · opportunity scouting via Data Science
hero.title: Pythia Scout
hero.subtitle: Translates the chaos of raw market data into a 0-100 viability score
hero.summary: Reuses an existing fleet of C# bots as the ingestion layer of a market-agnostic Data Science engine: every scraped payload passes through OmniShift (schema standardization) before reaching the predictive core in Python, which combines clustering, local NLP, and a weighted heuristic to decide whether something is a 'blue ocean' or just noise. Named after Pythia, the Oracle of Delphi who translated chaotic signals into clear prophecy.
hero.statusNote: The ingestion contract and the ViabilityScore formula are already designed; pipeline implementation hasn't started.

about.title: About the project
about.body: Born from a concrete need: a fleet of C# scraping bots already existed, what was missing was a central brain to decide what's worth chasing. Instead of rewriting the bots, Pythia Scout reuses them as the ingestion layer (Pipes and Filters) and builds the intelligence on top, in an architecture agnostic enough to serve any market vertical without touching the analytical core.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.body: Event-driven Pipes and Filters: each stage only knows the event it receives and the one it publishes. If the Data Science engine goes down for fine-tuning, the bots keep scraping and the messages stay safe in the queue — nothing is lost.
tree: C# bots (.NET 8)               extraction: scraping/APIs, publishes RawDataCollected
OmniShift (middleware)          validates the contract, standardizes schema, publishes DataNormalized
RabbitMQ                        the pipe between the three stages, routes by nicheHint
Python core (Polars + Ollama)   local NLP + clustering, computes the ViabilityScore
OpportunityScored event         satellites subscribe to the topic and trigger the business action

features.title: Key features
features.intro: Reuses what already exists, formalizes only what was missing: the brain.

items.title: Reuses the fleet, doesn't rewrite it
items.mechanic: The existing C# bots become the engine's Data Ingestion layer with no rewrite needed; OmniShift absorbs the job of standardizing different formats.

items.title: Composite score, not a magic number
items.mechanic: ViabilityScore is a weighted average of 4 variables (Demand, inverted Competition, Urgency, Technical fit), with the weight vector configurable per niche via Strategy Pattern.

items.title: Local NLP reads the client's pain
items.mechanic: An SLM via Ollama extracts Urgency and Demand straight from raw text (a complaint, a bid notice, a post), anchored by a system prompt with a strict scoring rubric to avoid hallucination.

items.title: Idempotency via hashing
items.mechanic: Every payload gets a SHA-256 content hash checked against Redis before any inference, so the same data never pays the AI cost twice.

items.title: Heuristic today, ML tomorrow
items.mechanic: The score calculation lives behind an IScoringStrategy interface; swapping the weighted formula for a Random Forest later doesn't break the entity's contract.

endpoints.title: The ViabilityScore Formula
endpoints.intro: Four variables, weights configurable per niche — the vector below is the B2B/industrial profile.

items.name: Demand (D)
items.what: Frequency and intensity of the reported problem

items.name: Competition (C)
items.what: Market saturation — enters the formula inverted (100−C)

items.name: Urgency (U)
items.what: Extracted via local NLP: frustration, hard deadline, reported losses

items.name: Technical fit (F)
items.what: Alignment with the ecosystem's delivery capacity

security.title: An Anti-Corruption Layer at the boundary
security.body: OmniShift acts as a contract validator: any malformed or unsigned payload is rejected before it reaches the main broker or the relational database. That isolates the predictive core from any dirty data coming from the bot fleet — the Python side never processes raw HTML or off-schema JSON, only what's already passed through the Anti-Corruption Layer.

meta.title: Talos Academy — Gustavo Vianna
meta.description: A no-black-boxes automation and AI learning platform: the Lyceum Methodology teaches the logic before the tool.

hero.eyebrow: Learning Platform · automation and AI fundamentals, no black boxes

security.title: What we deliberately avoid
security.body: The market standard for automation/AI courses pushes 'learn tool X in 2 hours' and get-rich-quick-with-AI promises — Talos Academy positions itself deliberately against that: architecture and data-security fundamentals before any interface, because the tool the market uses changes every cycle, but whoever understands the flow behind it never stays hostage to any single one of them.

hero.eyebrow: Management + Tycoon + Roguelike · remake of a classic
hero.title: Ultrafoot 26
hero.subtitle: Not just another spreadsheet manager: real crisis management for a football club
hero.summary: A remake of a classic football game that fuses the direct gameplay of a Management sim with the infrastructure and crisis depth of a Tycoon. The player takes on not just the role of coach, but of manager: political backstage, squad psychology, data security, and the real pressures of modern football.
hero.statusNote: Already live — desktop (Windows/Mac/Linux) and mobile, with a free and a paid tier.

about.title: About the project
about.body: The MVP prioritizes a solid core before any added complexity: a match engine with a real FIFA calendar, a fan-club membership system (revenue floats with team morale), home/away factors with age-based mental modifiers, and basic scouting. Tycoon-level complexity and random events come later, on top of a tested foundation — the architecture avoids heavy processing (no 3D match-physics engine) and uses simplified math simulation for CPU-controlled teams.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.body: Hexagonal + DDD isolates the game engine (the business rules) from the interface: calculating a match and its attribute modifiers never needs to open the game screen to be tested. Status effects (traumas, morale, sponsor pressure) are modeled as a list of modifiers on the Player entity — the match engine just sums base attributes and subtracts the active ones, with no knowledge of the business rule behind each. Domain events connect modules (marketing, health, morale) without coupling their code.
tree: Desktop frontend     Tauri + TypeScript — Windows, Mac, Linux
Mobile frontend      C# — native version
Game engine          Java 21 + Spring Boot, event-driven
Database             PostgreSQL — players, history, contract clauses

features.title: Standout mechanics
features.intro: Five systems that break from the football-manager status quo.

items.title: Persistent traumas and virtues
items.mechanic: A crushing collapse becomes a fixed condition on the involved players' profile — a -15% debuff removed only by a specific achievement, not by time passing.

items.title: Geographic factor
items.mechanic: Playing at altitude applies a real stamina-consumption multiplier, forcing squad rotation or consumable purchases.

items.title: Inter-club data warfare
items.mechanic: If a club's security infrastructure is weak, rival teams can intercept your scouts' reports — the same Zero-Trust logic applied to sports espionage.

items.title: Locker-room cliques
items.mechanic: The engine detects affinities (nationality, age, former club) and forms groups; punishing a group's leader tanks morale for everyone around him.

items.title: High-risk marketing
items.mechanic: Aggressive campaigns inject cash fast but create performance clauses — breaking the expectation doubles fan pressure and can void sponsorships.
